questions.stem: State what kind of object holds energy in a kinetic store.
questions.modelAnswer: Any object in motion holds energy in its kinetic store, sized by its mass and speed.

questions.stem: State the kinetic energy equation in words.
questions.modelAnswer: Kinetic energy equals one half multiplied by mass multiplied by speed squared.

questions.stem: Explain why forgetting to square the speed badly underestimates a moving object's kinetic energy.
questions.modelAnswer: The equation multiplies mass by the square of speed, so the speed contributes twice over. Using the bare speed once collapses the squared term, and for speeds above one metre per second the computed energy falls far below the true value held in the store.
